questions.content: The 1994 national mean daily hospital cost was $\$931$. A random sample of 30 Massachusetts hospital costs has mean $\$1,131$. Assume $\sigma=\$333$. Test at $\alpha=0.05$ whether the Massachusetts mean exceeded $\$931$.
questions.source: Assigments for Speaking of Statistics-Semester1-2014-2015/Assignment_Chapter 9 Hypothesis Testing Questions.docx

questions.content:
In 1990, mean annual passenger-vehicle mileage was 10.3 thousand miles. A random sample of 500 vehicles has mean 10.1 thousand miles; assume known $\sigma=6.0$ thousand miles.

a. Test $H_0:\mu=10.3$ versus $H_a:\mu\ne10.3$ at $\alpha=0.05$.

b. Construct a 95% confidence interval for $\mu$.
questions.source: Assigments for Speaking of Statistics-Semester1-2014-2015/Assignment_Chapter 9 Hypothesis Testing Questions.docx

questions.content: Last year's mean apartment price in Zhuhai was $\$8,650$/m² with known $\sigma=\$735$/m². A sample of 42 recent deals has mean $\$8,950$/m². At $\alpha=0.01$, test whether the mean price has increased.
questions.source: Assigments for Speaking of Statistics-Semester1-2014-2015/Assignment_Chapter 9 Hypothesis Testing Questions.docx

questions.content: A manufacturer claims mean light-bulb life is 1,520 hours. A random sample of 25 bulbs has mean 1,505 hours and sample standard deviation 86 hours. Assuming normal lifetimes, test at $\alpha=0.05$ whether the mean is less than 1,520 hours.
questions.source: Assigments for Speaking of Statistics-Semester1-2014-2015/Assignment_Chapter 9 Hypothesis Testing Questions.docx

questions.content:
A shipment may contain at most 2% defective electric can openers. In a random sample of 400, 11 are defective.

a. Test at $\alpha=0.05$ whether the defect rate exceeds 2%.

b. Report and interpret the observed significance level.
questions.source: Assigments for Speaking of Statistics-Semester1-2014-2015/Assignment_Chapter 9 Hypothesis Testing Questions.docx

questions.content:
Miranda samples 60 people from Adam's House at Harvard and finds 44 with piercings.

a. Test $H_0:p\le0.60$ versus $H_a:p>0.60$ at $\alpha=0.05$.

b. Identify a sampling concern.
questions.source: Assigments for Speaking of Statistics-Semester1-2014-2015/Assignment_Chapter 9 Hypothesis Testing Questions.docx

questions.content: In a blind taste test, 56 of 100 Diet Coke drinkers prefer Diet Pepsi. Test $H_0:p=0.50$ versus $H_a:p>0.50$ at $\alpha=0.05$, and state the consequence for the advertising claim.
questions.source: Assigments for Speaking of Statistics-Semester1-2014-2015/Assignment_Chapter 9 Hypothesis Testing Questions.docx

questions.content: Historically, 37% of cars failed a pollution standard. In a recent sample of 100 cars, 28% failed. Test at $\alpha=0.01$ whether cars have improved (a lower failure rate). State hypotheses in words and symbols, compute the statistic and p-value, and interpret the conclusion.
questions.source: Assigments for Speaking of Statistics-Semester1-2014-2015/Assignment_Chapter 9 Hypothesis Testing Questions.docx

questions.content:
ABZ Chemical Company claims its product contains no more than 4.0 fluid ounces of caustic material per gallon on average. The population standard deviation is known to be 1.3 ounces. A random sample of 100 containers has mean 4.5 ounces.

a. State $H_0$ and $H_a$ in symbols and words.

b. At $\alpha=0.01$, test whether the claim is false because the mean is too high.
The 2007 national mean daily hospital cost was $\$1,231$. A random sample of 25 Utah costs has mean $\$1,103$, with known $\sigma=\$252$. At $\alpha=0.05$, test whether Utah's mean was lower.

SAT scores are normal with known $\mu_0=500$ and $\sigma=100$. A sample of 25 students after preparation has mean 554.

a. Test at $\alpha=0.05$ whether the course changes the mean.

b. Would the conclusion change at $\alpha=0.01$?
The mean IQ of all college students is 109 with known $\sigma=15$. A random sample of 122 UIC students has mean 116. At $\alpha=0.05$, test whether UIC students have a higher mean IQ.
Last year's Zhuhai apartment price mean was $\$9,450$/m² with known $\sigma=\$1,035$/m². A sample of 47 recent sales has mean $\$9,850$/m². At $\alpha=0.01$, test whether the mean increased.

Last year's Zhuhai apartment price mean was $\$9,450$/m². A sample of 25 recent sales has mean $\$9,850$/m² and $s=\$1,035$/m². Assuming approximate normality, test at $\alpha=0.01$ whether the mean increased.

A manufacturer claims mean bulb life is 1,520 hours. A random sample of 40 bulbs has mean 1,505 hours and $s=86$ hours. Assuming normal lifetimes, test at $\alpha=0.05$ whether the mean is less than 1,520 hours.

In 2005, mean vehicle mileage was 15.3 thousand miles. A random sample of 50 vehicles in 2010 has mean 23.1 and $s=7.2$ thousand miles.

a. Test at $\alpha=0.05$ whether the 2010 mean differs from 15.3.

b. Construct a 95% confidence interval for the 2010 mean.

Reaction times are normal with mean 200 ms. Fourteen people taking a medication have mean reaction time 221 ms and sample variance $s^2=300$ ms². At $\alpha=0.05$, test whether the medication changes the population mean.

The historical mean IQ of entering freshmen is 110.3. A random sample of 36 current freshmen has mean 114.5 and sample variance $s^2=324$. At $\alpha=0.05$, test whether the current mean differs from 110.3.
In a blind taste test, 56 of 100 drinkers prefer Diet Coke. At $\alpha=0.02$, test whether more than half of all drinkers prefer Diet Coke.

An airline claims that more than 90% of lost luggage is recovered within 24 hours. In a sample of 122 travelers, 103 received luggage within 24 hours. At $\alpha=0.05$, test whether the airline overstated its recovery rate.

A sample of 50 regular-coffee drinkers has mean 4.35 cups/day and $s=1.20$; a sample of 40 decaffeinated-coffee drinkers has mean 5.84 cups/day and $s=1.36$. Assuming independent populations, test at $\alpha=0.01$ whether regular drinkers consume less and report the p-value.

At eight intersections, minor accidents before and after a traffic-light modification were:

| Intersection | A | B | C | D | E | F | G | H |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Before | 5 | 7 | 6 | 4 | 8 | 9 | 8 | 10 |
| After | 3 | 7 | 7 | 0 | 4 | 6 | 8 | 2 |

At $\alpha=0.05$, test whether the modification reduces the population mean number of accidents.
The target mean spindle diameter is 6 mm. State hypotheses for testing whether the production mean has deviated from the target.

questions.content:
For $H_0:\mu=98.6^\circ\mathrm{F}$ versus $H_a:\mu\ne98.6^\circ\mathrm{F}$, classify each outcome as a correct decision, Type I error, or Type II error:

a. $H_0$ is true but rejected.

b. $H_0$ is false and rejected.

c. $H_0$ is true and not rejected.

d. $H_0$ is false but not rejected.
